We use the stellar evolution code FuNS to compute the evolution of CD-3011223 up to the epoch when the two components come into contact and through the RLOF phase of the donor. With respect to our earlier study of the system PTF J2238+743015.1, we also include the transport of angular momentum due to magnetic instabilities (magnetic model). During the H-accretion phase, the effects of rotation in the accretor are negligible. In the "magnetic model", the angular momentum deposited by the accreted matter is very efficiently redistributed along the whole WD due to magnetic instabilities, so that the angular velocity of the accreted layers remains very low. During the He-accretion phase, the accretor experiences two very strong He-flashes, which result in the ejection from the binary system of a large part of the matter previously accreted. The system ends its life as a CO core capped by a massive He/C/O-envelope (Delta M_env ~ 0.194Msun) and an extremely low-mass companion, remnant of the donor, like in a rotating model not including the effects of magnetic field. The system CD-3011223 cannot be regarded as the potential progenitor of Supernova Ia. Such a conclusion applies also to all detached binary systems having similar masses of components and orbital periods.

arxiv.org/abs/2607.29128.title: Cosmological constraining power of the redshifts, heights, and angular clustering of weak gravitational lensing peaks
arxiv.org/abs/2607.29128.excerpt:
arXiv:2607.29128v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Weak gravitational lensing (WL) peaks probe non-Gaussian information of the large-scale distribution of matter that is not captured by two-point lensing statistics. We study the cosmological potential of the height distribution, redshift distribution, and angular clustering of high-valued WL peaks using a Bayesian inference approach that mimics a $\textit{Euclid}$ analysis. We use a forthcoming dark-matter-only hypercube, which varies cosmology in a ten-dimensional space, including evolving dark energy, neutrino mass, decaying dark matter, and the running of the scalar spectral index. We find the individual WL peak statistics to be complementary, as the redshift distribution best constrains the matter density, $\Omega_\mathrm{m}$, and the dark energy equation-of-state parameters, $w_0$, and $w_a$; the height distribution and angular clustering are most sensitive to the amplitude of the primordial power spectrum, $\ln(10^{10}A_\mathrm{s})$; while combining the three statistics allows us to also probe the baryon density, $\Omega_\mathrm{b}$, and the Hubble parameter, $h$. A comparison to the shear two-point correlation function demonstrates that WL peaks alone outperform the commonly used statistics, while even tighter constraints are obtained when combining all. Considering the 2-dimensional $\Omega_\mathrm{m}-\ln(10^{10}A_\mathrm{s})$ and $w_0-w_a$ parameter planes, we find that the redshift distribution outperforms the angular clustering and peak-height distributions. We study the impact of the smoothing scale and find that, typically, the smallest scales yield the best results and the figure of merit improves by a factor $\approx2$ when combining multiple scales.

arxiv.org/abs/2608.06453.title: Spectroscopic follow-up of compact object binary candidates from Gaia DR3: White dwarfs, neutron stars, black holes, and the parallax zeropoint
arxiv.org/abs/2608.06453.excerpt:
arXiv:2608.06453v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Astrometry and radial velocities (RVs) from Gaia DR3 yielded orbits for hundreds of thousands of binary systems, including several samples proposed to contain black holes (BHs), neutron stars (NSs), and white dwarfs (WDs). We present results of a systematic spectroscopic follow-up program targeting these objects. Beginning with a sample of 227 sources, we used a combination of archival data and many-epoch spectroscopic follow-up to characterize more than 200. We obtained 1292 high-quality RVs over a period of four years using the TRES and FEROS spectrographs, achieving a typical precision of 50 m/s and at least 10 RVs for 60 sources. We use these data to test the Gaia orbital solutions and tighten constraints on orbital parameters and component masses. Joint fitting of astrometry and RVs allows us to directly constrain flux ratios, verifying that undetected companions are genuinely dark. We find that ~60% of the astrometric candidates indeed host compact objects, including the two known Gaia BHs, 27 NS candidates, and a dozen massive WDs. We show that tight WD+WD binaries may masquerade as NSs within this sample. The spectroscopic candidates have lower purity: ~50% have spurious solutions, and a majority of the rest are post-mass-transfer binaries or hierarchical triples. Joint astrometry+RV fits of binaries with dark companions yield direct, parallax-independent distance measurements. Using 40 such systems, we measure the Gaia DR3 parallax zeropoint for astrometric orbital solutions. We find $Z=-0.0362\pm0.0053$ mas, consistent with the single-star zeropoint for sources of similar color and magnitude. These results will guide the selection of cleaner candidate samples from Gaia DR4, where a longer observing baseline will enable discovery of many more compact object binaries. RV follow-up will remain important for confirming individual systems, particularly those with extreme parameters.

arxiv.org/abs/2608.16656.title: Collisionless Shock Driven by a Supersonic Velocity Shear
arxiv.org/abs/2608.16656.excerpt:
arXiv:2608.16656v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: The long-term evolution of a relativistic collisionless velocity shear in an unmagnetized electron-positron plasma is investigated using a first-principle particle-in-cell simulation. The Alves instability converts the shear kinetic energy into thermal and magnetic field energy. The resulting pressures push the plasma, leading to the formation of collisionless shocks. The generated collisionless shocks would accelerate high energy particles, which is a possible solution to the injection problem of shear acceleration. In addition, the collisionless shocks generate a magnetic field turbulence that is required for the shear acceleration to work.

arxiv.org/abs/2609.08089.title: Multi-Height Spectropolarimetric Signatures of Magnetoacoustic Waves in Solar Plage
arxiv.org/abs/2609.08089.excerpt:
arXiv:2609.08089v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: We analyze high-cadence spectropolarimetric observations of solar plage obtained with the Visible Spectro-Polarimeter (ViSP) on the Daniel K. Inouye Solar Telescope (DKIST) to investigate low-chromospheric waves sampled by the Na I D1 5896 Angstrom and Ca II 8542 Angstrom lines. Observations were taken at an oblique viewing angle, providing sensitivity to transverse motions. Magnetic oscillations within plage elements exhibit significant line-of-sight (LOS) RMS amplitudes of approximately 9 G on average in the Na I D1 line, whereas the corresponding Ca II oscillations are only marginally above the noise level. Adaptive profile tracking provided line-core intensities and Doppler velocities, the weak-field approximation provided LOS magnetic fields, and non-LTE inversions provided mass densities and formation heights. Cross-spectral analysis shows velocity-intensity phase distributions coupled at -90 degrees, consistent with compressive oscillations. The velocity phases in Na I-Ca II indicate upward propagation and the phase speeds are predominantly sub-Alfvenic, consistent with slow magnetoacoustic waves. Although the slit geometry prevents a definitive identification of the tube eigenmode, the differing magnetic phase relationships suggest a height-dependent sausage-like behavior in the coupling between the magnetic and compressive perturbations. Additionally, our inferred wave fluxes are insufficient to heat active-region plage.

arxiv.org/abs/2609.13633.title: Examining Temporal Characteristics of GCRs in the AMS-02 era
arxiv.org/abs/2609.13633.excerpt:
arXiv:2609.13633v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: The energy spectra of Galactic cosmic rays (GCRs) serve as critical probes of their astrophysical origins and propagation mechanisms through the interstellar medium. Among the key physical processes shaping the observed spectra, solar modulation, driven by turbulent heliospheric magnetic fields and the variability of the solar wind, plays a dominant role in modifying GCR fluxes within the inner heliosphere. The recent release of time-dependent flux measurements for He, Li, Be, B, C, N, and O by AMS-02 provides unprecedented precision to investigate solar modulation phenomena. In this study, we demonstrate that Li, Be, B, C, N, and O nuclei exhibit solar modulation parameters consistent with those of protons (p) and He within a modified force-field approximation (FFA) framework incorporating rigidity-dependent modulation potentials. By positing that GCRs with the same charge-sign sharing the solar modulation parameters, we further forecast daily fluxes of Ne, Mg and Si from 2011 to 2020.

arxiv.org/abs/2609.19369.title: Characterizing the hierarchical structure of filaments I. On the origin of the length-mass (L-M) scaling relation
arxiv.org/abs/2609.19369.excerpt:
arXiv:2609.19369v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Aims. Filamentary structures in molecular clouds are widely recognized as fundamental components of star formation. Observations report a length-mass relation of the form $L \propto M^\alpha$ with $\alpha \simeq 0.5$. We characterize this relation in simulated molecular clouds and investigate the influence of hierarchical fragmentation and spatial resolution.
  Methods. We apply a two-step filament identification method to high-resolution 3D hydrodynamical and magnetohydrodynamical simulations from the SILCC-Zoom project, combining the Rolling Hough Transform with dendrogram-based segmentation for hierarchical decomposition. We analyze the resulting structures across multiple spatial resolutions.
  Results. The identified structures span column densities of $\sim 10^{21}$--$\sim 10^{23}\,\mathrm{cm}^{-2}$. Across multiple resolutions and, separately, the full hierarchical decomposition at the highest resolution, the ensemble exhibits a sub-linear $L-M$ relation close to $L \propto M^{0.5}$. When individual structures are traced across resolutions, the slopes remain sub-linear ($\alpha \simeq 0.45$--$0.70$), consistent with the geometric prediction $L \propto M^{0.5}$ of a fragmentation-driven random walk. In contrast, decomposing individual structures at the highest resolution yields a wide range of slopes ($\alpha \simeq 0.2$--$3$), peaking at $\alpha<1$. A simple toy model shows that this diversity arises from differences in the internal column-density distribution and segmentation geometry.
  Conclusions. Taken together, these results indicate that the average sub-linear length-mass relation with $\alpha \simeq 0.5$ is a robust property of the hierarchical structure and fragmentation occurring in molecular clouds.

arxiv.org/abs/2609.21324.title: Why most neutron star low-mass X-ray binaries accrete transiently: an evolutionary study of transient and persistent phases
arxiv.org/abs/2609.21324.excerpt:
arXiv:2609.21324v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: A neutron star (NS) low-mass X-ray binary (LMXB), in which an NS accretes matter from a low-mass donor star, is an ideal source for probing some fundamental aspects of physics and astronomy, such as strong gravity, superdense matter, and the accretion-ejection processes. However, to reliably achieve these goals, one must adequately understand NS LMXBs, including why some accrete persistently and others transiently. Focused models, such as those based on a thermal-viscous instability in the accretion disk, are considered to explain transient accretion. However, broader perspectives, including which LMXB parameter values and phases cause transients and why there are more transients than persistents, remain poorly understood. Here, our computation of the long-term evolution of NS LMXBs addresses these questions, providing insight into LMXB parameters and phases, naturally producing more transients than persistents, and being partially consistent with the known properties of observed sources. For example, we typically find a greater fraction of persistent phase at lower orbital periods from the LMXB evolution computation, which is somewhat consistent with observations. However, a lack of full consistency calls for improving the aforementioned focused models, and our computations provide a new way to discriminate among these models.

arxiv.org/abs/2609.26998.title: N/O-enhanced chemical enrichment by massive stars: the interplay of optically-thick winds and rotation
arxiv.org/abs/2609.26998.excerpt:
arXiv:2609.26998v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Recent JWST observations have revealed a sample of high-$z$ galaxies with highly enhanced N/O abundance ratios, $\log\rm (N/O)\gtrsim -1.1$. Strong optically-thick winds of rotating massive stars going through the Wolf-Rayet (WR) phase provide a viable explanation for such N/O enhancements, supported by the direct spectroscopic WR signatures discovered in a few galaxies. Such strong winds are also needed to reproduce the single WR stars in the Small Magellanic Cloud (SMC). Here, we compute the metal yields of massive ($\sim 20-100\ \rm M_\odot$), metal-poor stars using two sets of MESA single stellar evolution models with and without optically-thick winds in a dense grid of metallicities ($Z_\star\sim 0.001-0.0045$) and initial spins ($\omega\equiv\Omega/\Omega_{\rm crit}\sim 0-0.7$). Considering an initial spin distribution based on observations of O-type stars in the SMC, we find that both sets produce strong N/O enhancements up to $\rm \log(N/O)\sim 0.1$ within a few Myr after a starburst. The models with optically-thick winds undergo a rapid transition from high N/O to the `normal' state of $\rm \log(N/O)\sim -1.5$ at $t\sim 3-4$ Myr driven by C/O-rich winds, while the transition is slower and weaker without optically-thick winds. The optically-thick-wind scenario can reproduce the nebular C, N, O, and He abundance patterns of three representative high-$z$ galaxies showing direct WR signatures: RXCJ2248-ID, Sunburst Arc, and MARTA 4327, with stellar metallicities and ages similar to those inferred from SED-fitting. This can be interpreted as a coherent evolution sequence captured before ($t\lesssim 3$ Myr), during ($t\sim 3-4$ Myr), and after ($t\gtrsim 5$ Myr) the transition. In contrast, the optically-thin-wind-only scenario ejects much less C and O via winds and cannot reproduce Sunburst Arc and MARTA 4327. The yields are available at https://zenodo.org/records/22897057.

arxiv.org/abs/2610.03343.title: Discovery of thermal radio recombination line emission toward the high-mass protostar IRAS18162$-$2048
arxiv.org/abs/2610.03343.excerpt:
arXiv:2610.03343v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: The physical conditions within the innermost few tens of au of high-mass protostars ($M_*>8~M_\odot$) remain largely unexplored. At these scales, ionised emission may trace photoionised gas, accretion disks, or the base of protostellar jets. We search for ionised emission in the form of radio recombination lines (RRLs) in high-mass star-forming regions. We use archival data from the Atacama Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA) interferometer in band 6 ($\sim$1.3 mm) with a resolution of $\theta_\mathrm{beam}\sim53~\mathrm{mas}\times42~\mathrm{mas}$ to examine the high-mass protostar IRAS18162$-$2048, driving source of the Herbig-Haro (HH) objects HH80-81. We detect, for the first time in this protostar, the thermal emission of the RRL H30$\alpha$ ($\mathrm{rest~frequency}=231.90093$ GHz). The ionised emission is spatially unresolved in our observations, but we estimate an emitting region $\lesssim50$ au at the source distance of 1.4 kpc. The H30$\alpha$ line profile is broad and spectrally resolved with a Local Standard of Rest velocity of $\sim-14~\mathrm{km~s^{-1}}$ (i.e., $\sim-26~\mathrm{km~s^{-1}}$ blue-shifted with respect to the systemic velocity of the cloud) and a full width at half maximum of $\sim82~\mathrm{km~s^{-1}}$. These observations suggest that the H30$\alpha$ line is tracing outflowing blue-shifted material in the well-known radio jet from this object. This detection opens the possibility of detailed studies of the kinematics and physical properties of ionised jets.

arxiv.org/abs/2503.19660.title: Effect of ultralight dark matter on compact binary mergers
arxiv.org/abs/2503.19660.excerpt:
arXiv:2503.19660v3 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: The growing catalogue of gravitational wave events enables a statistical analysis of compact binary mergers, typically quantified by the binary merger rate density. This quantity can be influenced by ambient factors, following which, in this work we have investigated the impact of dark matter environment on the merger statistics. We construct a baseline astrophysical model of eccentric and quasi-circular compact binary mergers and extend it by incorporating a model of ultra light dark matter, which affects the orbital evolution of binaries through accretion and dynamical friction. Our analysis of the merged population of binary progenitors demonstrates that, compared to the baseline model, ULDM can potentially alter the merger statistics around an optimal combination of ambient density $\lesssim10^4 \textrm{GeV}/\textrm{cm}^{3}$ and eccentricity $\sim 0.5$. A comparison with the gravitational wave data from the GWTC-3 catalogue provides crucial insight into potential observational signatures of the ULDM in merger events, leading to possible constraints on the existence and density of dark matter distribution in galaxies.

arxiv.org/abs/2603.27080.title: Optimized numerical evolution of perturbations across sharp background trajectory turns in multifield inflation
arxiv.org/abs/2603.27080.excerpt:
arXiv:2603.27080v3 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: Features in the primordial power spectrum require numerical methods that are both accurate and scalable across the wide class of multifield inflationary models that produce them. Sharp turns in the background trajectories, induced by either potential or geometric effects, render these computations particularly challenging. In this work, we introduce an efficient method for evolving primordial scalar fluctuations, requiring time steps comparable to those used for the background evolution. We demonstrate that the method accurately tracks perturbations through rapidly turning trajectories in arbitrary field-space geometries, enabling systematic exploration of spectral features across diverse multifield scenarios. Our approach scales robustly to large numbers of degrees of freedom, providing a reliable computational framework for probing regimes that significantly depart from slow-roll or slow-turn dynamics.

arxiv.org/abs/2603.28689.title: Probing soft signals of gravitational-wave memory with space-based interferometers
arxiv.org/abs/2603.28689.excerpt:
arXiv:2603.28689v3 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: Gravitational-wave displacement memory is a remarkable, ubiquitous prediction of general relativity that has not yet been detected. Unlike the oscillatory components of gravitational waveforms, displacement memory is associated with soft gravitons and provides the leading low-frequency observable of its parent event. Analogous soft signals may also be associated with velocity and integrated-displacement memory. The simple, universal spectral shapes of soft waveforms provide effective templates for matched filtering and parameter estimation. In this paper, we investigate the detection prospects for such soft memory signals with future space-based laser interferometers. As realistic examples, we examine the infrared spectral features of gravitational waves from moderately relativistic nonspinning compact binary scattering and comparable-mass quasi-circular, nonprecessing black hole mergers. In both cases, the low-frequency spectrum can be described by a soft displacement-memory waveform with finite-frequency corrections. Using the adopted instrumental-noise models, simulated Bayesian parameter-estimation analyses show that a single LISA-like detector can constrain the memory amplitude and arrival time for signals with matched-filter signal-to-noise ratios of order 10. BBO Stage 1 could measure null displacement memory from sufficiently loud stellar-mass compact binary mergers. We also evaluate the detectability of an idealized stochastic background of soft displacement-memory signals. These results establish gravitational-wave bursts with memory as concrete targets for space-based interferometers.

arxiv.org/abs/2605.11332.title: Reviving primordial black hole formation in slow first-order phase transitions
arxiv.org/abs/2605.11332.excerpt:
arXiv:2605.11332v3 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: Large curvature perturbations generated during slow first-order phase transitions are a promising source of primordial black holes. However, recent analyses suggested that the mechanism is ruled out once the density contrast and the formation threshold are evaluated in the same gauge. In this work, we show that this mechanism remains viable: after a supercooled transition, reheating can be sufficiently slow that the Universe enters an early matter-dominated era, during which even small overdensities grow and collapse into primordial black holes.

arxiv.org/abs/2605.13955.title: Exploring neutrino loss with diffuse astrophysical neutrino fluxes
arxiv.org/abs/2605.13955.excerpt:
arXiv:2605.13955v2 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: We study the sensitivity of the diffuse high-energy neutrino flux observed in IceCube to new-physics effects resulting in an exponential flux attenuation along the trajectory, such as invisible neutrino decay or new interactions with the background encountered during propagation. We argue that, even though the sources and production redshifts of these astrophysical neutrinos are unknown, conservative energy-conservation arguments allow to severely constrain neutrino loss in most scenarios beyond the strongest existing bounds. By performing a fit to the High-Energy Starting Events from IceCube, we quantify the bounds and study their variation with the energy dependence of the attenuation, the assumed redshift distribution of the neutrino sources, and whether the attenuation affects neutrinos exclusively or no. We also show that including an energy-dependent attenuation at the level allowed in the fit may impact the determination of the spectral index of the diffuse flux.

arxiv.org/abs/2605.15146.title: Matter Flavor Conversion Mediated by Pseudo-Sterile States as the Possible Origin of Neutrino Oscillation Anomalies
arxiv.org/abs/2605.15146.excerpt:
arXiv:2605.15146v2 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: Neutrino oscillation experiments present anomalous results across a vast range of baselines and energies. Here we show that a 3+1 scenario in which sterile neutrinos feel a novel matter potential $V_s$ proportional to background density of ordinary or (asymmetric) dark matter is able to explain several anomalies. At low-energies ($E\lesssim$ 1 TeV) the model behaves as an effective 3-flavor NSI-like scheme among active flavors and eliminates the tension between the two LBL experiments NOvA and T2K provided that the potential is negative and the two sterile mixing angles $	heta_{14}$ and $	heta_{24}$ are non-zero. A further indication in favor of a negative non-zero potential comes from the anomalous excess of $
u_e$-like events observed in Super-Kamiokande atmospheric neutrinos, which, in the new scenario is explained by a modification of the 3-flavor resonance at few GeV. A high energies ($E\gtrsim $ 1 TeV) the new framework reveals its 4-flavor nature and produces a resonant behavior at $E \simeq$ 10 TeV as hinted at by IceCube. We identify an irreducible 3-level dynamics generating a new resonance in the $(
u_e, 
u_\mu)$ sector intertwined with two conventional resonances in the $(
u_e, 
u_s$) and $(
u_\mu, 
u_s)$ systems. The novel amplification mechanism manifests with the emergence of effective mixing angles in matter ($	heta_{12}^m$ or $	heta_{13}^m$) involving active neutrinos. The scenario requires values of $f = V_s/|V_{NC}| \sim -20 $, $\Delta m^2_{41} \sim 60 $ eV$^2$, $|U_{e4}|^2\simeq \sin^2	heta_{14} \simeq 0.01-0.03$ and $|U_{\mu4}|^2 \simeq \sin^2	heta_{24}\simeq 10^{-4}-10^{-3}$. Such a very small size of $|U_{\mu4}|^2$ eliminates the tension between IceCube and the other $
u_\mu$ disappearance searches. The model can be directly probed by KATRIN, which is very sensitive to the electron-sterile neutrino admixture in the region of high $\Delta m^2_{41}$.

arxiv.org/abs/2605.24081.title: Production of Leptophilic Bosons in Ultradegenerate Relativistic Matter
arxiv.org/abs/2605.24081.excerpt:
arXiv:2605.24081v2 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: Neutron stars (NSs) are powerful factories for new particles with masses up to the 100~keV range. These compact stars contain significant amounts of protons, electrons, and muons. We deduce the emission rates for new scalar, vector, and pseudoscalar bosons coupling to electrons and muons. For muonic vector bosons, in addition to direct emission from leptons in incoherent scatterings with the medium, a competing channel is the coherent excitation of the lepton population electromagnetically induced by incoherent hadronic scatterings - an effective in-medium coupling. For muonic scalar bosons, emission from the effective in-medium coupling to electrons is always dominant due to their relativistically boosted emission. Pseudoscalars can only be emitted through incoherent leptonic scatterings. If protons are superconducting, the scalar and vector energy loss rates scale as $T^4$, the pseudoscalar ones as $T^6$, to be compared with $T^8$ for neutrino losses by the modified Urca (MUrca) process. For normal-conducting protons, the damping of transverse photons implies instead scalings with a power $T^{11/3}$ for scalars, and $T^{17/3}$ for pseudoscalars; vectors, emitted by nonrelativistic protons in the nonsuperconducting regime, still scale as $T^4$. Our results can be used to constrain the leptophilic coupling strengths through observed NS cooling ages.

arxiv.org/abs/2605.24094.title: Neutron Star Bounds on Muonic Fifth Forces from Picometer to Meter Scales
arxiv.org/abs/2605.24094.excerpt:
arXiv:2605.24094v2 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: Testing muonic fifth forces is difficult because muons are scarce in ordinary matter. However, they are abundant in neutron stars. We show that this population responds coherently to electromagnetic fluctuations induced by proton and electron collisions, emitting the fifth-force mediator and cooling the star. This energy loss constrains $g_{X\mu}\lesssim 10^{-13}$ for scalars with $m_\phi\lesssim 100$ keV and vectors with $10^{-5}\,\mathrm{eV}\lesssim m_V\lesssim 100$ keV, far more strongly than SN 1987A cooling. Vector forces at smaller $m_V$ deplete muons, suppressing the coherent response. Cooling from incoherent muon scattering still constrains $g_{V \mu}\lesssim 2.5\times 10^{-12}$ for $1.3\times 10^{-7}\,\mathrm{eV}\lesssim m_V\lesssim 10^{-5}$ eV. Together, these bounds provide the most sensitive probes of muonic interactions across a broad range of parameters.

arxiv.org/abs/2605.28752.title: Inflation with vector fields revisited: non-Gaussianities
arxiv.org/abs/2605.28752.excerpt:
arXiv:2605.28752v3 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: {We revisit the resulting bispectrum of inflation with kinetic-coupled vector fields by organizing the dynamics in terms of $h$, which measures the vector kinetic contribution relative to that of the scalar field. We derive a low-energy effective field theory (EFT) and evaluate the bispectrum of the curvature perturbation for the large-$h$ regime. For $h\gg1$, the entropic perturbation becomes heavy and can be integrated out; the remaining curvature mode has an imaginary sound speed and undergoes transient growth before horizon crossing. In contrast to the $h\ll1$ regime, where transfer from the vector sector persists outside the horizon and produces a local-type contribution enhanced as $h^2N_K^3$, we find that the bispectrum signals are controlled by the matching parameter $x\simeq1.63Ah$, where $A<1$ is a numerical factor remaining dependent on the UV-to-EFT matching prescription. As a result, in addition to the known flattened-enhanced signals scaling as $x^3$, a flattened-enhanced signal scaling as $x^2$ and a pronounced local projection scaling as $x$ are present. The bispectrum therefore distinguishes vector-supported inflationary dynamics even for an exactly isotropic background.

arxiv.org/abs/2609.33596.title: Stochastic gravitational-wave background from self-interacting superradiant clouds
arxiv.org/abs/2609.33596.excerpt:
arXiv:2609.33596v2 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: Gravitational-wave (GW) observations offer a powerful probe of new fundamental fields. One well-motivated source is black hole (BH)--boson cloud systems, in which an ultralight scalar field forms a cloud around a rotating BH via superradiance and emits long-lived nearly monochromatic GWs. In this work, we compute the stochastic GW background (SGWB) from such systems, extending previous work by including scalar self-interactions, and discuss its detectability with next-generation ground-based GW detectors. We find that self-interactions can suppress the SGWB and thereby relax existing LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA constraints inferred from null searches. Namely, the LIGO detectors at design sensitivity are insensitive to a SGWB produced by scalar fields with a decay constant $f_\mathrm{s} \lesssim 3\times 10^{17}$ GeV, independently of the scalar field mass. Looking ahead, we show that a moderately self-interacting cloud can still produce a detectable SGWB with next-generation detectors. Under conservative assumptions, for a decay constant $f_\mathrm{s} = 10^{17}$ GeV, the Einstein Telescope (ET) will be sensitive to scalar masses in the range $\sim[10^{-13.0},10^{-11.8}]$ eV, while Cosmic Explorer (CE) will be sensitive to scalar masses in the range $\sim[10^{-13.2},10^{-11.7}]$ eV. We also find that the minimum decay constants that still yield a detectable SGWB for ET and CE are $f_\mathrm{s}\sim 6\times10^{16}\,$GeV and $\sim 3\times10^{16}\,$GeV, respectively.

arxiv.org/abs/2609.33869.title: Heavy Higgsino Dark Matter With Low Reheating in View of the LZ High-Recoil Event
arxiv.org/abs/2609.33869.excerpt:
arXiv:2609.33869v2 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: We show that a heavy higgsino $\tilde h$ with mass $m_{\tilde h}\sim0.1~{\rm PeV}$, which can be made consistent with the recent LUX-ZEPLIN event avoiding constraints from direct and indirect detection, can account for the present cold dark matter abundance of the universe, if the reheating temperature is bounded as $T_{\rm rh}\lesssim 595~{\rm GeV}$. These values can be achieved by a possible out-of-equilibrium decay of a modulus $\phi$ with mass $m_{\phi}\gg m_{\tilde h}$ and a non-vanishing branching ratio into $\tilde h$'s which plays a decisive role in reducing $T_{\rm rh}$ below its upper limit via the non-thermal $\tilde h$ production. The modulus $\phi$ can be identified with the scalar component of the goldstino superfield which is involved in the generation of the $\mu$ parameter of MSSM (with $\mu\simeq m_{\tilde h}$) via the Giudice-Masiero mechanism.

arxiv.org/abs/2609.38769.title: Kilopixel Performance of the Kinetic Inductance Detectors for the Terahertz Intensity Mapper
arxiv.org/abs/2609.38769.excerpt:
arXiv:2609.38769v2 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: We characterize a flight-grade array of lumped-element kinetic inductance detectors (LEKIDs) developed for the long-wavelength module of the Terahertz Intensity Mapper (TIM). From an 864-pixel science array, we select 490 well-isolated resonators spanning the focal plane and readout band and measure their thermal response, optical responsivity, and noise using a ZCU111-based multitone readout system intended for flight. The thermal and optical response of the detector population is consistent with previous single-pixel measurements and can be described by Mattis-Bardeen theory under the influence of a change in Cooper pair or quasi-particle density. Under increasing blackbody loading, the measured noise transitions from a thermal generation-recombination-dominated floor to photon-noise-limited scaling, with the majority of detectors achieving photon-noise-limited operation by approximately 400 fW incident power, with a median detector noise-limited NEP of $NEP_{det} = 1.1\times10^{-17} W \sqrt{Hz}$. The measured photon-noise scaling implies a median optical efficiency of approximately 0.67, indicating additional unknown loss sources between the detectors and blackbody radiator, tentatively attributed to losses in the waveguide. These results demonstrate that the TIM LEKID architecture retains the required sensitivity when scaled to kilopixel-class arrays; the principal remaining challenges are array-level tone optimization, resonator tracking, and identification of frequency-domain collisions.

arxiv.org/abs/2610.12552.title: A Burst of Reionization in the Dark Ages
arxiv.org/abs/2610.12552.excerpt:
arXiv:2610.12552v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Primordial overdensities at small scales can be significantly larger than those observed at large scales. As a result, they can collapse much earlier, at redshifts $z \sim 100$. In these collapsed halos, stars and black holes can form, where they can then contribute to an early reionization of the universe. If this epoch is temporary, the free electrons will recombine yielding a low level of ionization leading into cosmic dawn. This contributes to the optical depth of the universe, and adds more weakly to low-$\ell$ polarization signals of ionization compared to later sources. We study the effects of a redshift-localized source of reionization $\Delta \tau_{burst}$ in the context of a broad suite of cosmological data to constrain this scenario, finding a preference of approximately $\sim 2-2.5\sigma$ for a new contribution. Regardless of Planck reprocessing used (PR3 - SRoll2+plik or PR4 - LoLLiPoP+CamSpec/HiLLiPoP), the results are consistent, favoring a new contribution $\Delta \tau_{burst} \sim 0.012$ ($0.001 < \Delta \tau_{burst} < 0.022$ at 95\%) and a similar total optical depth $\tau \sim 0.073$. The precise era of reionization is somewhat discrepant depending on the higher-$\ell$ reprocessing used, with HiLLiPoP favoring $z\sim 45$, CamSpec $z\sim 100$ and plik $z\sim 165$. If such a source is present at $40\lesssim z\lesssim150$, LiteBIRD should be able to detect it, while Simons Observatory should also constrain it.

arxiv.org/abs/2610.12553.title: A Single Line-Emitter Identified in an Unbiased Search with JWST/NIRSpec: Multi-Object Coronagraphy for Slitless Spectroscopy
arxiv.org/abs/2610.12553.excerpt:
arXiv:2610.12553v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We report the detection of a previously unknown object with a single emission line within the Hubble Ultra Deep Field, using a new JWST NIRSpec technique called Multi-Object Coronagraphy for Slitless Spectroscopy (MOCSS) with the G140M/F100LP observing mode. The MOCSS technique involves opening almost all the shutters on the NIRSpec microshutter array, while simultaneously closing the shutters that lie on top of known low redshift objects, facilitating a wide field slitless spectroscopic search without contamination from bright objects. This observational technique has enabled the detection of a strong emission line in four different dither positions and in two position angles, and thus cannot be artificial. This line is detected at 1.60 $\rm \mu m$ with a line flux of $[2.5\pm 0.3]\times10^{-18} \rm erg\ s^{-1} cm^{-2}$ and a FWHM of $13.2\pm2.0${\AA}, and does not correspond to any known source with some of the deepest HST and JWST imaging in existence. Based upon the absence of imaging detection, we place a lower limit on the observed frame equivalent width (EW) of 7620{\AA} on this object, which strongly limits the number of possible lines that this line can be. Given the wavelength, an EW limit that is near the ceiling of expectation, and the lack of other lines in the bandpass, this line cannot be easily explained by [OII] at $z=3.29$, [OIII] at $z=2.20$, H$\alpha$ at $z=1.44$, and Ly$\alpha$ at $z=12.16$. We discuss possible AGN and transient phenomena that could explain the finding.

arxiv.org/abs/2610.12562.title: The accretionally heated atmospheres of protoplanets and brown dwarfs
arxiv.org/abs/2610.12562.excerpt:
arXiv:2610.12562v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The ranks of accreting planets and brown dwarfs are growing. To help interpret their spectra, we study how accretion affects a planet's atmosphere. The atmosphere is irradiated from above by whatever nonthermal radiation from the accretion shock does not directly escape into space. This accretional heating drives a temperature inversion. Even relatively slow accretion, corresponding to mass doubling times longer than system ages, can raise temperatures by many hundreds of Kelvin at ambient pressures of order millibars. The heated atmosphere radiates an optical/infrared excess. For environments that are not too dusty, the excess concentrates in molecular lines that trace the heated layer. Thus an accretionally heated atmosphere may be distinguished by its muted absorption bands. Irradiation from the accretion shock also changes the chemical composition of the atmosphere, further altering spectra. Atmospheric retrievals promise to map out the deposition of accretional energy, helping to decide between ''hot'' and ''cold'' start modes of planet formation.

arxiv.org/abs/2610.12577.title: The road to $H_0$, $\Omega_m$, and $w$ with a global neutrino-telescope network
arxiv.org/abs/2610.12577.excerpt:
arXiv:2610.12577v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The newly measured correlation between the neutrino and X-ray luminosities of Seyfert galaxies has yielded the first neutrino-based measurement of the Hubble constant. Building on this result, we forecast the reach of a global neutrino-telescope network by 2030, utilizing full-sky IceCube exposures combined with KM3NeT-ARCA and Baikal-GVD. We find that this 2030 configuration sharpens the neutrino-measured Hubble constant from today's $H_0 = 66^{+44}_{-37}$ to $H_0 =66^{+15}_{-13}$ km s$^{-1}$ Mpc$^{-1}$. Additionally, we project that the disk-corona slope of the neutrino X-ray luminosity relation ($L_\nu\propto L_X^\beta$) will reach $\beta=0.72\pm0.04$, enabling a $\geq \!5\sigma$ exclusion of the calorimetric value $\beta=1$. Finally, we show that, if a high-redshift population of neutrino sources, such as JWST's "little red dots," is identified and obeys the same luminosity relation, we can obtain a new independent measurement of the matter density $\Omega_m$ and the dark energy equation-of-state parameter $w$.

arxiv.org/abs/2610.12591.title: When dust growth takes over: the origin of dust in post-reionization galaxies
arxiv.org/abs/2610.12591.excerpt:
arXiv:2610.12591v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The post-reionization epoch ($z\sim4$-6) marks a critical phase in galaxy evolution, during which galaxies rapidly assemble their stellar mass, enrich their interstellar medium, and build up substantial dust reservoirs. The physical processes responsible for such rapid dust enrichment remain uncertain. We investigate the dust enrichment history of the ALPINE-CRISTAL-JWST (ACJ) sample using the semi-analytic galaxy formation model GAlaxy Evolution and Assembly (GAEA), which follows galaxy assembly, chemical enrichment, and dust evolution. We select model galaxies matching the observed stellar masses, star formation rates, and metallicities of the ACJ sample, compare their dust properties with observed scaling relations, and trace their enrichment histories and environments. The model reproduces the observed dust mass-stellar mass relation and the dust-to-stellar mass, dust-to-gas, and dust-to-metal ratios as functions of stellar mass and metallicity. Reproducing these constraints requires efficient dust growth in the interstellar medium; stellar dust production alone cannot account for the observed dust reservoirs, even under the most optimistic assumptions. The combination of stellar mass, star formation rate, and metallicity provides a good predictor of galaxy dust content. Our model suggests rapid dust build-up consistent with the previously noted rapid metal enrichment, with evidence for a transition around $z\sim8$-9 below which dust growth becomes the dominant dust formation channel. Finally, ACJ-like galaxies preferentially reside in locally overdense environments, suggesting that environment may have contributed to their accelerated evolution. Taken together, these results support rapid and coupled stellar, metal, and dust build-up in ACJ galaxies during the post-reionization era.

arxiv.org/abs/2610.12595.title: Nailing down the Hubble constant value through time delay cosmography: A 3% measurement from SN Refsdal
arxiv.org/abs/2610.12595.excerpt:
arXiv:2610.12595v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We present the first inference of the Hubble constant and matter density parameter from a strongly lensed supernova (SN) by exploiting the mass model of a galaxy cluster enhanced by an extended surface brightness reconstruction. This has resulted in the most precise H0 measurement from a single strong lens so far, outperforming the 3.9% result from the lensed quasar DES J048-5354. Building upon the mass model of MACS J1149.5+2223 relying on image positions only, we incorporate the surface brightness distribution of the SN Refsdal host, to infer some cosmological parameter values within a flat LCDM framework. We consider two cosmological parameterizations, with either H0 and $\Omega_m$ or H0 alone treated as free parameters. We explore four different mass-model realizations to assess some of the systematic uncertainties associated with the constraint weighting and source reconstruction. Although known as one of the main systematic effects, we deliberately keep the cluster total mass parametrization fixed to that of the previously published point-like mass model to enable a fair comparison. This reveals that incorporating 77,000 HST pixels reduces the uncertainty on the inferred value of H0 by a factor of 2.0. Our final measurements are $H_0=65.0^{+2.0}_{-1.8}$ km/s/Mpc and $\Omega_m=0.30^{+0.08}_{-0.09}$, in agreement with previous results from lensed SNe. This corresponds to a substantially improved precision, reaching a remarkable 3.0% uncertainty on the value of H0. The contributions of the uncertainties on the lens total mass and on the measured time delays to the final H0 error are now comparable, indicating that future improvements will depend on more precise time-delay measurements and continued control of systematic effects. With sub-percent time-delay values reachable at cluster-scale, this mass model approach has the power to lead to unprecedentedly precise H0 measurements.

arxiv.org/abs/2610.12600.title: "Mega-Earths" are likely an artifact of stellar activity
arxiv.org/abs/2610.12600.excerpt:
arXiv:2610.12600v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Empirical relations and planet formation simulations suggest an upper mass limit for rocky planets of $\sim$10M$_{\oplus}$, as cores above this will almost certainly undergo runaway gas accretion. Nevertheless, a small number of planets appear to have densities consistent with rocky Earth-like compositions above this threshold, indicating that unusual formation and evolutionary scenarios are capable of producing extremely massive rocky planets called "Mega-Earths." However, all of these planets orbit active stars with log$R'_{HK}$ $>$-4.75. We find a <1$\%$ probability that all literature ultra-massive rocky planets would coincidentally orbit such active stars, and find no astrophysical reason to expect Mega-Earths to preferentially form around active stars. We therefore conclude that Mega-Earths are artifacts of stellar activity, and we question the reliability of Gaussian Processes to enable mass measurements for rocky planets around active stars.

arxiv.org/abs/2610.12632.title: The Fast & Fourier: Using neural operators to speed up radiative modeling of protoplanetary disks
arxiv.org/abs/2610.12632.excerpt:
arXiv:2610.12632v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Edge-on protoplanetary disks provide a spatially resolved view of the vertical distribution of icy planetary building blocks, but inferring their relative abundances requires radiative-transfer (RT) modeling with multiple anisotropic scattering. Each model costs $10^{1}$-$10^{3}$ CPU hours, which precludes principled Bayesian inference and homogeneous, population-scale analyses. We develop and validate a fast and reusable surrogate for Bayesian inference with ice-bearing edge-on disk models. We train a Fourier Neural Operator on a grid of RADMC-3D spectra. The network maps disk parameters and analytic physical input fields to the spectrum, using mixed-resolution spectra. We use the surrogate in an explicit-likelihood nested sampler and validate it on held-out simulations and synthetic recovery tests with TARP coverage. Finally, we use it to retrieve the disk structure and ice abundances of ESO-H$\alpha$ 569 from its spectral energy distribution. The surrogate reproduces the RADMC-3D spectra with a median error of 4.84%. We recover synthetic parameters without detectable bias and with nominal coverage. For ESO-H$\alpha$ 569, the posterior favors a massive ($M_{\rm gas}=0.028^{+0.015}_{-0.011}\,M_\odot$), nearly edge-on ($i=79.8^{+5.2}_{-2.4}$ deg) disk consistent with the image-plus-SED model of Wolff et al. (2017). Its ice abundances and cavity size remain weakly constrained by broadband data alone. The marginal spectrum-evaluation speed-up is $\sim10^{9}$-$10^{10}$. Neural-operator emulation makes full posterior inference feasible within the adopted model and training prior. Key posterior points should still be checked with high-fidelity RT models. By drastically cutting evaluation time, this approach enables for the first time homogeneous population studies of ices in disks, which new JWST surveys can capitalize on to map the range of compositions within planetary nurseries.

arxiv.org/abs/2610.12648.title: Dust-driven vertical shear instability in an isothermal shearing box: I. Turbulence and gas dynamics without dust feedback
arxiv.org/abs/2610.12648.excerpt:
arXiv:2610.12648v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The classical vertical shear instability (VSI) is a baroclinic instability that arises from height-dependent azimuthal velocities and is a leading candidate for driving anisotropic turbulence in discs with extended vertical modes. The classical VSI requires fast cooling times and radial temperature gradients, which are absent in an isothermal stratified (barotropic) setup. We investigate the dust-driven vertical shear instability in an isothermal, stratified shearing box, where the VSI is generated by drag forces acting on the gas due to dust rather than radial thermal stratification. We construct two-fluid (gas+dust) vertically stratified equilibria including dust diffusion and use these profiles to initialise 2D (radial-vertical) hydrodynamical simulations with FARGO3D. To separate dust-driven vertical shear instability (DVSI) from drag instabilities, we employ a dust-analogue model in which dust-induced drag on the gas is prescribed as a time-invariant and height-dependent acceleration, such that the underlying spatial distribution of the dust is assumed to be constant. The DVSI grows from regions of strongest vertical shear away from the midplane, exciting predominantly radially short, vertically extended disturbances (large k_x/k_z) and producing banded structures in the perturbed azimuthal and vertical velocities during the linear phase. In the nonlinear regime, the instability saturates via a Kelvin-Helmholtz-like parasitic instability that breaks the coherent vertical-shear modes into smaller-scale eddies, which balance the growth of the vertically extended modes, driving sustained vertical stirring. Dust-driven vertical shear can drive anisotropic turbulence and vertical mixing in an isothermal model without invoking global thermal gradients and could play an important role in the stratified streaming instability.

arxiv.org/abs/2610.12677.title: The GAPS programme at TNG LXXXII. The first atmospheric investigation of the gas giant WASP-13b at high resolution with GIARPS
arxiv.org/abs/2610.12677.excerpt:
arXiv:2610.12677v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Low-density transiting gas giant exoplanets are key benchmarks for atmospheric studies. Despite their large-scale heights, many of them remain poorly characterised. We present the first atmospheric investigation at high-resolution of the inflated (R$_\mathrm{p}$$\sim$1.4 R$_{\mathrm{J}}$), hot Jupiter (T$\sim$1500$ \mathrm{K}$) WASP-13 b aiming at constraining its atmospheric composition and refine its orbital geometry. We analysed four transits observed with GIARPS at the TNG. Updated stellar and planetary parameters were re-derived from the most precise literature values, and a new Rossiter-McLaughlin analysis was performed to measure the projected spin-orbit angle ($\lambda$) and stellar rotational velocity ($v\sin{i_\star}$). Atmospheric signals were searched using high-resolution spectroscopy, both with cross-correlation and single-line analyses, targeting key atomic and molecular species (e.g. \ion{He}{I}, H$\alpha$, \ion{Na}{I}, H$_2$O, CO). We find a well-aligned orbit ($\lambda$ = 2.7$\pm$1.1$^\circ$) and $v\sin{i_\star}$ = 4.5$\pm$0.1 km s$^{-1}$, improving upon previous constraints. No significant atmospheric absorption is detected in either VIS or NIR data. Injection-and-recovery tests exclude an isothermal atmosphere with metallicity [M/H]$\lesssim$10$\times$[M/H]$_\odot$ and simultaneously a grey cloud top pressure P$_{\rm cloud}\gtrsim10$ mbar, under the assumption of chemical equilibrium. WASP-13 b appears to belong to the class of low-density hot Jupiters with weak or featureless transmission spectra, most likely shaped by the presence of high-altitude clouds. Although a highly metal-enriched atmosphere cannot be fully excluded, current evidence disfavours this scenario. Further observations with next-generation facilities will be essential to characterise the atmospheric properties of this challenging target.

arxiv.org/abs/2610.12715.title: Exploring Case B I: The Footprints of Hidden Radiation Fields in H I Balmer Decrements
arxiv.org/abs/2610.12715.excerpt:
arXiv:2610.12715v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Theory predicts that H I emission from photoionized clouds should lie close to the Case B limit established by Menzel and Baker, and observations of nearby nebulae have largely confirmed this expectation. However, recent observations of more distant high-redshift systems have revealed a small fraction with striking departures from Case B. What additional physics might be at work in these objects? This paper is part of a series exploring the physical processes that can produce such departures. In Paper I (D26), we show that Case B remains remarkably robust over a broad range of physical conditions, consistent with observations of nearby nebulae. Here, we explore one additional ingredient: a soft, non-ionizing radiation field. Such a continuum can strongly perturb the Balmer spectrum. The largest effects occur for radiation fields resembling log(Teff K)\sim 3.2-4.2 blackbodies, where photoexcitation from the metastable 2s level alters the hydrogen level populations and subsequent radiative cascade. The resulting Halpha/Hbeta and Hgamma/Hbeta ratios follow a different trajectory from dust reddening, allowing the two effects to be distinguished using multiple Balmer lines. In unresolved systems, a cool source located near the line-emitting gas may provide an additional radiation field distinct from the hot stars responsible for ionization. Balmer decrements may therefore carry information about otherwise hidden components of the radiation field surrounding the emitting gas.

arxiv.org/abs/2610.12729.title: Bridging Theory and Observation: Synthetic Far-infrared Insights into Star Formation Efficiency
arxiv.org/abs/2610.12729.excerpt:
arXiv:2610.12729v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The star formation efficiency per free-fall time ($\epsilon_{\rm ff}$) quantifies how efficiently giant molecular clouds (GMCs) convert gas into stars and is often observed to be orders of magnitude lower than expected for free-fall collapse. Observers typically estimate $\epsilon_{\rm ff}$ by mapping far-infrared (FIR) dust emission to infer gas surface densities ($\Sigma_{\rm gas}$) and counting embedded protostars, assuming simplified lifetimes and masses. Using the fiducial STARFORGE radiation-magnetohydrodynamics simulation of an $M_{\rm cl} = 2\times10^4 M_\odot$ GMC that self-consistently models star cluster formation and stellar feedback, we generate synthetic FIR observations and apply the same methodologies used in GMC surveys to investigate this discrepancy. We present the first $\epsilon_{\rm ff}-\Sigma_{\rm gas}$ analysis in a fully feedback-regulated GMC simulation that resolves the formation of stellar systems. Our synthetic measurements reproduce the low observationally inferred efficiencies, showing that feedback-regulated star formation naturally produces $\epsilon_{\rm ff} \sim 1-3\%$ without requiring extreme initial conditions. We also find that $\epsilon_{\rm ff}$ varies strongly over a GMC's lifetime, suggesting that much of the observed scatter reflects evolutionary sampling rather than intrinsic cloud-to-cloud differences. Finally, by comparing observational and simulation definitions, we show that methodological assumptions introduce systematic biases, with a transition near $\log \Sigma_{\rm gas} \approx 2.3 M_\odot {\rm pc}^{-2}$ that depends on resolution. Above this threshold, the smoothing of dense structure increases both the inferred free-fall time and enclosed gas, with the latter dominating and suppressing $\epsilon_{\rm ff}$. Below the threshold, the discrepancies are primarily driven by star formation rate assumptions.

arxiv.org/abs/2610.12743.title: Predicted state-to-state collisional rate coefficients from neural networks
arxiv.org/abs/2610.12743.excerpt:
arXiv:2610.12743v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Molecular spectra observed in the interstellar medium are commonly analyzed using non-local thermodynamic equilibrium models, which requires accurate state-to-state collisional rate coefficients. Close-coupling calculations become prohibitively expensive for transitions from highly excited rotational states, therefore available datasets are often truncated at low initial states and temperatures; and since each new system also requires an accurate ab initio potential energy surface, many detected molecules have no collisional data. We employ two machine learning strategies to predict rotational state-to-state rate coefficients of molecules included in the train set beyond the range of initial states and temperatures computed so far, and predicting those of a molecule absent from training and validation sets. Feed-forward neural networks are trained on state-to-state de-excitation rate coefficients of 24 linear molecules colliding with para-H2. Scheme 1 includes all systems in the train+validation set, with 70%, 80%, and 90% initial-state boundaries and a 90% temperature boundary. Scheme 2 is trained on 22 systems described only by transition and molecular properties, and predicts two excluded systems, CS and CF+, whose astrophysical impact is explored with non-LTE calculations. For the 90% boundary, Scheme 1 predicts 99.4% of the test transitions within a factor of 2, and no prediction deviates from the reference value by more than a factor of 4.7. This model was used to complete 18 datasets. Scheme 2 reproduces the rate coefficients of two excluded systems within a factor of 3 for more than 92% of their transitions. Both schemes provide near-instantaneous complements to close-coupling calculations: Scheme 1 extends the range of a molecule already included in the training set with high accuracy, while Scheme 2 gives a reasonable first estimate for a molecule that has not been studied.

arxiv.org/abs/2610.12880.title: Decomposing the Kinematics of SNR G180.0-01.7 with Medium-Resolution Spectra
arxiv.org/abs/2610.12880.excerpt:
arXiv:2610.12880v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The exceptionally large angular diameter and intrinsic optical faintness of the Galactic supernova remnant (SNR) G180.0-01.7 (S147) have historically hindered a comprehensive spectroscopic census of its filamentary structure. We present the first dedicated medium-resolution (R ~ 7500) spectroscopic study of S147 using the LAMOST Medium-Resolution Spectroscopic survey of Galactic Nebulae (MRS-N). By implementing multi-Gaussian decomposition on the H$\alpha$, [NII], and [SII] emission complexes and applying combined spectroscopic and spatial criteria, we disentangle the shock-ionized filaments of the SNR from the pervasive foreground and background Diffuse Ionized Gas (DIG). Our analysis reveals a distinct bimodal radial velocity distribution for the SNR: a low-velocity population tracing the decelerated forward shock at a dense cavity wall, and a high-velocity population (with absolute radial velocities of ~ 70 $\pm$ 30 km/s) corresponding to ejecta within a low-density cavity. The co-existence of these populations provides kinematic evidence for the "supernova-in-a-cavity" scenario. Furthermore, we detect enhanced [SII]/H$\alpha$ ratios in the DIG along the eastern and northern boundaries of the remnant, signaling shock compression of the ambient interstellar medium and highlighting remnant's multifaceted feedback.

arxiv.org/abs/2610.12943.title: In-flight Timing Calibration of the Follow-up X-Ray Telescope on Board the Einstein Probe
arxiv.org/abs/2610.12943.excerpt:
arXiv:2610.12943v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: After the launch of Einstein Probe (EP), pulsars are observed to calibrate the timing system of the onboard Follow-up X-ray Telescope (FXT) by measuring the times of arrival (TOAs). FXT has two independently operating modules, namely FXTA and FXTB, each equipped with the Wolter-I optics and the pnCCD camera. For scientific observations, each pnCCD has three distinct readout modes that differ in frame cycles, the full frame mode (FF, 50 ms per frame), the partial windowed mode (PW, 2.2 ms per frame), and the timing mode (TM, 23.68 $\mu$s per row, 9.4352 ms per frame). Thus, 1RXS J170849.0--400910 with the spin period of 11 s is observed in FF, PSR B1509--58 (150 ms) in PW, and Crab pulsar (33 ms) in TM as well as PSR B1821--24 (3.05 ms) and PSR B1937+21 (1.56 ms). The TOAs of these pulsars measured by FXTA and FXTB are compared with the results of NICER, and for Crab pulsar with the Jodrell Bank Monthly Ephemeris (JBE). Results verify that the timing system of FXTA and FXTB in FF, PW, and TM modes are consistent with each other, and are in good alignment with NICER. The measured advance of the Crab pulsar's main peak relative to JBE is $357^{\pm14(stat)}_{\pm54(sys)} \mu$s in FXTA and $394^{\pm14(stat)}_{\pm67(sys)} \mu$s in FXTB. Based on measurements of PSR B1821--24 and PSR B1937+21, the preliminary absolute timing accuracy is estimated to be 6 $\mu$s for FXTA and 31 $\mu$s for FXTB in TM mode. Additionally, the systematic delay of FXTA timing results relative to FXTB is found to be $20^{\pm19(stat)}_{\pm21(sys)} \mu$s.

arxiv.org/abs/2610.12947.title: Global analysis of tensor mode helicity
arxiv.org/abs/2610.12947.excerpt:
arXiv:2610.12947v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: A detection of helicity in a primordial gravitational-wave background (GWB) would provide compelling evidence for parity violation in the early universe and point toward physics beyond the standard picture of inflation. Since big bang cosmology is not time translation invariant, we identify that the so-called ``regular'' and often-neglected ``irregular'' solutions are independent degrees of freedom that can in principle carry different, even opposite, helicities. We note that this possibility complicates the interpretation of a measured net helicity. To determine the sensitivity of various GW detector configurations to helicity, we introduce a universal helicity efficiency coefficient that provides a unified geometric description of helicity sensitivity across gravitational-wave detectors which generalizes and improves previous estimators. We apply this helicity efficiency coefficient to estimate the sensitivity of a range of future GW experiments to helicity across twenty orders of magnitude in frequency assuming a fully helical background with an amplitude just below the current constraints.

arxiv.org/abs/2610.12968.title: The Neptunian Final Parsec Problem: How Inertial Waves Enable Neptunes and Gas Giants to Survive Tidal Migration
arxiv.org/abs/2610.12968.excerpt:
arXiv:2610.12968v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Observations indicate that some hot Neptunes and Jupiters underwent high eccentricity migration (HEM). A longstanding issue facing HEM theory remains, however: in order to shrink their orbits by ${\sim}1{-}2$ orders of magnitude, planets must dissipate ${\gtrsim}10{\times}$ more orbital energy than is contained in their structural binding energy. Previous work suggests that excitation of planets' fundamental modes (''$f$-modes'') at very high eccentricities, $e{\sim}$0.99, can shrink semi-major axes by ${\sim}$an order of magnitude (${\sim}5{\rightarrow}0.5$ au) while safely bleeding tidal energy to space. We examine how planets traverse the remaining order of magnitude in orbital shrinkage, $a{\sim}$0.5${\rightarrow}$0.05 au, which still poses a danger for Neptunian planets due to their lower binding energies (their ''final parsec'' problem). To assess whether tidally-migrating Neptunes balance their energy budgets, we perform coupled orbit/structure calculations tracking their frequency-dependent tidal response under inertial waves (IWs). We show that tidal radius inflation at moderate eccentricities sweeps Neptunes' fundamental modes back into resonance with tidal forcing; only a small amount of tidal heat relative to a Neptune's binding energy is needed to drive this $f$-mode excitation. This excitation of Neptunes' $f$-modes may offer a route to safe circularization, provided the $f$-mode dissipates without harming the planet. In contrast, eccentric gas giants ($e{\sim}0.9$) circularize without drama over ${\sim}$Gyr. Our theory predicts that warm Neptunes on a HEM track ($a{\gtrsim}0.1 \ \mathrm{au}, \ e{\gtrsim}0.8$) should be rare, in opposition to warm gas giants and lower eccentricity Neptunes. Observational confirmation of our predictions would constrain the interior structures of Neptunian planets via tidal theory.

arxiv.org/abs/2610.12974.title: An Ultraviolet Instrument on the Habitable Worlds Observatory: Considerations and Capability Trades on the Multi-Object, Integral-field, and High-resolution modes of a potential UVI
arxiv.org/abs/2610.12974.excerpt:
arXiv:2610.12974v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The Habitable Worlds Observatory (HWO) is NASA's next-generation astrophysics platform, delivering transformative capability in the search for life and study of the origins of the universe. Amongst the instruments under consideration for HWO is a multi-purpose ultraviolet spectrograph and imager that provides a deep toolbox for some of the most pressing science investigations of the next several decades. In this paper, we present a basic draft model of a potential UVI, including a multi-object spectrograph, far ultraviolet imager, high resolution spectrograph, and integral-field spectrograph. The draft designs for these channels of the UV instrument serve as a basis for a general discussion of the instrument architecture and design challenges, while also identifying potential trades, enhancements, and other considerations that the HWO project will need to address as it moves into the formulation phase. We conclude with a presentation of several scientific simulations that have helped guide the capabilities of the draft design. This paper is intended to serve as a summary of UV instrument modes, technology, and potential design ahead of planned instrument studies in the late 2020's, and then Phase A in the early 2030's.

arxiv.org/abs/2610.13011.title: ASKAP Monitoring of the Rubin Deep Drilling Fields
arxiv.org/abs/2610.13011.excerpt:
arXiv:2610.13011v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: In the past decade, time domain astronomy surveys across the multi-messenger spectrum have developed "alert streams" which circulate observational information in real-time to the wider astronomical community. Despite this being standard practice for optical, gamma-ray and gravitational wave time domain astronomy for several years now, this kind of infrastructure has not yet been deployed at-scale for radio telescopes. We are conducting a long-term monitoring program that targets the Rubin Deep Drilling Fields using the Australian SKA Pathfinder (ASKAP). The primary goal of this program is to provide serendipitous radio observations of all objects of interest in these fields, and circulate that information in as close to real-time as possible. In this manuscript we outline the survey plans and status, the infrastructure we have developed to disseminate this information and an initial data release comprising 5 months of ASKAP observations of each field (although only 3 months overlaps with Rubin) conducted on an approximately 10 day cadence with a noise level of $\sim 60\,\mu$Jy. As part of this data release, we present updated high-cadence radio light curves to the tidal disruption event AT2018hyz and the supernova SN2024abfo along with the discovery of two new radio variables, a possible tidal disruption event ASKAP J095711.5+051205 and an in-progress extreme scattering event ASKAP J005026.4-422958. The scientific results from this program along with the infrastructure developed to acquire them will lay the foundation for the integration of future radio imaging surveys into the broader multi-messenger alert stream, leading the way for major facilities such as the Schmidt Observatory System and the SKA.

arxiv.org/abs/2610.13039.title: Redshifted Cool Gas in the Disturbed HI Disk of the Starburst Dwarf NGC 4214
arxiv.org/abs/2610.13039.excerpt:
arXiv:2610.13039v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We report redshifted cool gas toward the central star-forming region of the nearby starburst dwarf galaxy NGC 4214. HST/COS spectra show low-ionization absorbers redshifted relative to the systemic velocity, most clearly in SII ($\Delta v=19.8\pm2.6\ {\rm km\,s^{-1}}$) and supported by MgII ($\Delta v=30.3\pm3.0\ {\rm km\,s^{-1}}$), while PII remains tentative ($\Delta v=7.5\pm3.4\ {\rm km\,s^{-1}}$). The Keck/HIRES spectra also reveal a redshifted CaII absorption component ($\Delta v=25.6\pm1.5\ {\rm km\,s^{-1}}$). Because the absorption is detected against the central UV or optical continuum, the gas must lie in the foreground of the star-forming region and is moving away from the observer and toward the background UV source in projection. A VLA--THINGS HI spectrum extracted at the COS position within one VLA beam also shows a redshifted neutral component at $v_{\rm hel}=329.2\pm0.9\ {\rm km\ s^{-1}}$, offset by $38.2\pm1.3\ {\rm km\ s^{-1}}$ from systemic and by $27.6\pm1.0\ {\rm km\ s^{-1}}$ from the dominant local HI component. The FAST HI mapping further reveals an extended, kinematically disturbed neutral disk, with residual structures relative to a warped-disk model. Together, the redshifted UV absorption, the redshifted HI component, and the disturbed large-scale HI velocity field show that the central anomalous cool gas is observed in a galaxy with a disturbed extended neutral disk. This geometry suggests that the redshifted cool gas may trace inflow or recycled fallback toward the central region, although warped-disk or non-circular disk motions cannot be fully excluded.

arxiv.org/abs/2610.13062.title: A Relationship Between Fast Radio Burst Dispersion Measure and Host Galaxy Inclination
arxiv.org/abs/2610.13062.excerpt:
arXiv:2610.13062v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: It is commonly thought that fast radio bursts (FRBs) trace star formation, and that they are produced by magnetars. Both hypotheses imply that their sources are hosted primarily (but not exclusively) in galactic disks. Although there is evidence in that direction, it has yet to be shown conclusively. In addition, a tension exists with the fact that at least one FRB source is found in a globular cluster far from the disk of the host. If FRBs originate primarily in disks, the galaxy orientation could leave an impression in the sample of observed FRBs, either as a selection bias against FRBs in edge-on galaxies or as a correlation with DMHost. Statistical tests against the inclinations of FRB host galaxies, derived from parametric morphology applied to optical and near-infrared imaging, can search for these effects. Such a search requires an adequately large sample of known FRB hosts that have been imaged to a sufficient depth, while estimates of DMHost also require the redshift of each host to be known. These conditions are best met in the Commensal Real-time ASKAP Fast Transient (CRAFT) survey sample of FRB host galaxies, for which the majority have been imaged at optical wavelengths with FORS2 on the Very Large Telescope (VLT). Here these data are fitted with the morphology software GALFIT to derive the elliptical axis ratio q (a proxy for inclination) for 34 hosts from the CRAFT sample, detected with ASKAP and followed up with VLT imaging. We find no bias against FRB detections from edge-on galaxies; instead, we uncover a new relationship between the inclination of an FRB host galaxy and DMHost. This is consistent with a primarily disk-based origin for CRAFT FRBs. Using this relationship we are able to reduce the scatter of the host sample about the Macquart relation by 40%, demonstrating a new empirical method for estimating DMHost that requires only deep optical imaging.

arxiv.org/abs/2610.13127.title: Star Cluster Ecology VIII. -- Dynamically Forming S-Type and $\alpha$Centauri-like Systems
arxiv.org/abs/2610.13127.excerpt:
arXiv:2610.13127v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Aims: To analyse the impact of dynamically formed binaries emerging naturally from various star cluster environments on already established planetary systems. Methods: Numerical simulations replicating the star-forming region NGC 1333 are conducted. We consider three models, each using identical cluster realisations and simulation parameters. The cluster itself is initially sub-virial and fractally distributed. Model~A assumes planetary systems are initially in mean motion resonance. In Model~B, the same planetary systems are moved out of resonance, but remain intrinsically stable. Finally, Model~C removes all planets from the simulation. Ten independent realisations are integrated per model until 30 Myr. Results: Dynamically formed binaries emerge at similar rates across models, indicating planets play little role in their formation. We also find a higher production rate of wide binaries compared to previous numerical studies which we attribute to the sub-virial and sub-clustered initial conditions. S-type and binary S-type planetary systems naturally emerge in our simulations, while P-type systems are rare. For Model~A, the fraction of S-type or binary S-type systems is f_{\rm S}=0.02 and $f_{\rm Bin,\, S}=0.05, respectively. Rogue planets originating from a binary system are ejected with a substantially larger velocity than those around singletons. Planet-star collisions and planet capture events occur disproportionately within binary systems. Finally, several \alphaCentauri-like systems emerge in our simulations, suggesting that the nearest stellar system to the Sun may have a dynamical origin.

arxiv.org/abs/2610.13173.title: Formation Dynamics of a Rotating Solar Spicule-like Event and Associated Energy-Mass Transport
arxiv.org/abs/2610.13173.excerpt:
arXiv:2610.13173v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We performed three-dimensional radiative magnetohydrodynamic(3D RMHD) simulations in an upward-directed (positive-polarity) open magnetic field with an initial background strength of 10 G. We identified vortex-associated spicule-like events and carried out a detailed analysis of one representative event. Prior to the formation of this spicule-like event, a photospheric vortex appears and twists the magnetic field lines, then develops upward into higher atmospheric layers, forming a magnetic tornado system. This event is generated during this process. At the periphery of this magnetic tornado, twisted magnetic field lines with negative vertical components reconnect with both external positive-polarity background fields and central positive-polarity fields. The magnetic reconnection sites rise and rotate together with the developed magnetic tornado, and many jet-like substructures in this event are closely associated with plasma upward ejections from these reconnection regions. A vertical force analysis shows that, for this event, plasma uplift in the photosphere and lower chromosphere is dominated by the pressure-gradient force, whereas in the upper chromosphere, the Lorentz force gradually becomes dominant. At a height of about 4 Mm above the solar surface, this event produces a mean upward mass flux density on the order of $10^{-7}~{\rm kg~m^{-2}~s^{-1}}$ and a mean upward Poynting flux density of approximately $525~{\rm W~m^{-2}}$. The wave-mode decomposition results show that the energy transport associated with the rotational spicule-like event is dominated by the Alfv\'en mode. Alfv\'en waves, fast-mode waves, and slow-mode waves carry energy into the lower corona in an approximate ratio of $10:7:3$.

arxiv.org/abs/2610.13182.title: Flux Evolution of PSR B0540--69 and the Spectral Energy Distribution of its Pulsar Wind Nebula
arxiv.org/abs/2610.13182.excerpt:
arXiv:2610.13182v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The young Crab-like pulsar PSR B0540--69, located in the Large Magellanic Cloud, underwent a spin-down rate transition (SRT) in 2011 December, after which its pulsar wind nebula (PWN) was reported to brighten up to 2018. In this work, we extend the study of its X-ray and $\gamma$-ray flux evolution through 2026 by combining observations from multiple X-ray instruments with data from the Fermi Large Area Telescope, thereby constructing a flux history of the PSR$+$PWN system spanning more than two decades. We find that the enhanced X-ray luminosity of the PSR$+$PWN system has persisted for more than 14 yr after the SRT, up to early 2026, whereas the pulsed X-ray flux remains unchanged across all epochs. This confirms that the brightening originates from the PWN. In the $\gamma$-ray band, neither the pulsed nor the non-pulsed flux shows any detectable long-term variation between 2008 and 2025. Together, these results imply that the additional spin-down energy released at the SRT has been continuously injected into the PWN over decades, placing strong constraints on the energy budget and physical mechanism of the transition. Combining the non-pulsed X-ray and $\gamma$-ray fluxes measured here with previously published radio-to-UV data, we further construct a broadband spectral energy distribution of the PWN, which shows properties markedly different from those of the Crab Nebula.

arxiv.org/abs/2610.13183.title: Simulation Study of Reconstruction of Cosmic Ray Extensive Air Shower with Thermal Neutron Detected by ENDA
arxiv.org/abs/2610.13183.excerpt:
arXiv:2610.13183v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: In the investigation of the "knee" region within the cosmic ray energy spectrum, extensive air shower (EAS) reconstruction by using different EAS secondary particles are of paramount importance for energy determination and composition separation and finally measurement of energy spectrum of different cosmic ray composition. The Electron-Neutron Detector Array (ENDA) is designed to detect thermal neutrons generated in the ground by high energy hadrons which constitute the "backbone" of EAS and carry vital information regarding the primary cosmic rays. At present, ENDA-64, consisting of 64 detectors, is employed inside the Large High Altitude Air Shower Observatory (LHAASO). This work simulates the response of ENDA and investigates the lateral distributions of thermal neutrons. A comparison of the NKG and double-exponential functions for describing this distribution using MC simulation data shows that the double-exponential function is more accurate. The mean difference between fitted and measured thermal neutron density is within ~ 6%. Meanwhile, the thermal neutron density at 10 m from the shower axis, $\rho_n$, depends mainly on the sum of all hadrons energy or the number of high-energy hadrons. The relationship between $\rho_n$ and EAS hadron energy or the number of high-energy hadrons can be well fitted by a linear function on a log scale. This work is fundamental for energy determination and composition separation with hybrid detection by using ENDA in the near future.

arxiv.org/abs/2610.13200.title: Detailed study of HD 219134: a benchmark K-dwarf with a compact planetary system
arxiv.org/abs/2610.13200.excerpt:
arXiv:2610.13200v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Space missions such as CoRoT, Kepler, and TESS have transformed asteroseismology and its synergies with exoplanet science. We revisit the nearby K-dwarf HD 219134 to investigate the tension between asteroseismic and interferometric radii, update its fundamental parameters, and reconstruct the rotational, magnetic, and atmospheric evolution of the system. We combine forward asteroseismic modeling with seismic inversions to assess systematics from non-seismic constraints, radius measurements, and surface modeling. The revised stellar properties are then used for rotational evolution, stellar-wind, and high-energy irradiation calculations. Seismic inversions rule out the most recent interferometric radius, while the asteroseismic and spectroscopic results are compatible with the 2019 interferometric measurement. We obtain $M=0.779\pm0.015_\mathrm{(stat)}\pm0.006_\mathrm{(sys)}\ M_\odot$, $R=0.753\pm0.005_\mathrm{(stat)}\pm0.002_\mathrm{(sys)}\ R_\odot$, and an age of $8.92\pm0.89_\mathrm{(stat)}\pm0.19_\mathrm{(sys)}$ Gyr. These systematics include only non-seismic constraints; literature combined uncertainties from physical inputs and surface effects are $0.007M_\odot$, $0.002R_\odot$, and $0.81$ Gyr. Rotational and wind modelling shows that standard magnetic braking is broadly compatible with the present-day rotation and angular-momentum loss. Weakened braking gives a closer match but challenges standard wind-loss scalings. The inferred X-ray history suggests early stripping of the innermost planets, while the outer planets likely retained part of their primordial envelopes; HD 219134d experienced only moderate erosion. The apparent radius discrepancy likely reflects underestimated uncertainties in previous interferometric analyses rather than an astrophysical inconsistency.
